title: Line diff engine on similar
problem_context:
- The diff viewer needs per-line diff information to render: old and new lines paired, each marked unchanged, removed, added, or modified, numbered from the line offset, with inline changes on modified lines.
- The component also needs to know where changes sit, so it can fold the unchanged lines around them.
- The reference is `src/compute-lines.ts`; alignment follows `similar`, so the TypeScript tests are a source of cases, not expected output.
plan_guidance:
- Every in-scope requirement binds acceptance alongside the criteria.
- Defaults generally follow react-diff-viewer, per stakeholder steering: character comparison and inline changes are on unless the consumer chooses otherwise.
- The engine carries no presentation; views, folding, and styling belong to the component and theming work units.
- Risk signal carried from the epic: implementation-complexity.
- The crate is `dioxus-diff-viewer`; its public names use the requirement terms (unchanged, removed, added, modified, inline changes, compare method, line offset, line ending change), not the reference's `DEFAULT`, `diffLines`, or `disableWordDiff`.
status_summary: Implementation complete. The `dioxus-diff-viewer` crate lives at `rust-dioxus/` and carries the engine: `line_diff` takes two texts and LineDiffOptions and returns a LineDiff of paired entries plus the positions holding a change, with no presentation. All 19 tests pass, clippy is clean, and rustfmt is applied. Both worker to-do advice records are addressed: WORK:advice-nj1vrndsnf (Reference porting hazards) and WORK:advice-zaj371p040 (Test strategy for the engine). Next is post-work review by the Architect, the Code Whisperer, and the Rust Tester; the in-scope requirements stay where they are until that review's final stage advances them.

body:
**Commits**
- `9a0699b`: line change and line number requirements drafted DREAMED for this unit's scope.

**Decisions**
- The Rust Roundup UI group (Dioxus Coder, Dioxus UI Patterns, Appshell Expert, Forms Expert) is left off this unit because the engine has no UI; the mission names it for the crate as a whole, and the component work unit takes it.

**Observations**
- `.project/architecture/` does not exist yet, so the first architecture record for this crate (the candidate architecture work-ready asks for) needs the Architect's placement choice first; low severity.

**For the next worker**

content: REQT-hmsfnfe5wc (Line marking) defers alignment to `similar`'s line diff, but `similar` keeps line terminators inside line tokens, so a last line without a trailing newline never matches the same text followed by one; the reference line addition and line deletion cases would show their unchanged `test` line as modified.
evidence:
`similar-3.2.0/src/text/abstraction.rs:164-190` (`tokenize_lines`) includes `
` or `
` in each line token. A scratch probe of `TextDiff::from_lines("test", "test
    newLine")` returned Delete `test`, Insert `test
`, Insert `    newLine`; `"a
b"` against `"a
b
c"` returned Equal `a
`, Delete `b`, Insert `b
`, Insert `c`. The reference expects `test` unchanged at `test/compute-lines-test.ts:34-65` and `:67-98`. REQT-9tze98pt6g (Trailing whitespace) trims each text's end, as `src/compute-lines.ts:149-151` does, which guarantees both last lines lack terminators. `TextDiffConfig::newline_terminated` affects only unified diff generation (`similar-3.2.0/src/text/mod.rs:407-411`, `:436-439`).

presentation.title: Line terminators break line matching
presentation.synopsis: `similar` keeps newlines inside line tokens, so an unterminated last line never matches the same line followed by a newline.
presentation.context:
Re-orienting: line marking defers alignment to `similar`'s line diff.
Catch-up:
- Where: REQT-hmsfnfe5wc (Line marking) in the diff viewer requirements.
- Purpose: decides which lines read as unchanged.
- Situation: trimmed texts end without a newline.
- Goal: equal line text reads unchanged.
presentation.key_points:
- `similar` line tokens include `\n` or `\r\n`.
- Trimming each text's end leaves its last line unterminated.
- The reference line addition and deletion cases would show `test` as modified.
- The requirement's words hold while its intent fails.
presentation.resolution_points:
- `compare-without-terminators`: amend REQT-hmsfnfe5wc so lines are compared by their text without line terminators.
- The same amendment settles whether `\r\n` and `\n` endings count as a difference.
presentation.substance: Requirements coverage and contract correctness: the literal requirement yields spurious modified lines on common inputs.
presentation.specificity_reasoning: The requirement hands alignment wholly to `similar` without stating how line identity is compared.

addressed_details.response: REQT-hmsfnfe5wc (Line marking) now compares lines by their text without line terminators, so `\r\n` and `\n` endings align as unchanged. Differing endings stay visible through REQT-rtwn1qresp (Line ending changes), REQT-4zyjfjrhd3 (Line ending chips), and REQT-8y5fp2aarz (Line ending chip color).

content:
No test strategy is recorded, and greenfield work-ready requires one. Proposed strategy:
- Output-based tests against the engine's public entry point, with no Dioxus runtime involved.
- One focused test per in-scope child requirement, named as a plain-English behavior carrying the REQT id.
- Reference cases from `test/compute-lines-test.ts` as a table, each named by its reference case; a case that differs asserts the engine's own output and states its cause beside it.
- Property tests: each side's line texts rejoin to that side's trimmed input, and each side's line numbers run contiguously from the offset plus one.

Sketch:
```
rows = compute("test", "test\n    newLine", defaults)
assert rows == [unchanged(old 1, new 1, "test"), added(new 2, "    newLine")]   // REQT-hmsfnfe5wc
rows = compute("Hello World", "My Updated Name\nAlso this info", compare = words)
assert rows[0] is modified and its old-side tokens rejoin to "Hello World"      // REQT-xzc8n354h1
property(old, new, offset): old-side texts joined by newline == old.trim_end()
```
evidence: `coder/coder.codingDiscipline.reqts.md:129` lists an articulated test strategy as work-ready condition (d). The work unit carried no work_advice before this pass. Reference cases at `test/compute-lines-test.ts:5-412` cover trailing whitespace, addition, deletion, modification, inline changes, default and word compare methods, disabled inline changes, and line offset. `rust-tester/rust-tester.SKILL.md:105-107` ranks output-based testing first where the code under test is pure.

Output-based tests call the public entry point with no Dioxus runtime involved; one focused test per in-scope child requirement carries that REQT id in its doc comment; the reference cases run as a table named by each reference case, with two further tests recording the cases that differ and their causes per WORK:crit-rdjdbfyxnt; and both property tests hold, for line-text reconstruction and for contiguous numbering from the offset. The sketch's own assertions are among the passing tests.

content: WORK:crit-rdjdbfyxnt (reference cases) allows only carried over or differing because of `similar`'s alignment, but some reference expectations are defects of the reference itself, leaving a worker to port the defect or fail the criterion.
evidence: `test/compute-lines-test.ts:273-276`, `:335-338`, and `:407-410` expect `diffLines` of [0, 2] for two rows. Tracing `src/compute-lines.ts:197-211` with `:251`: the nested call that reads the paired added line increments `counter` before the outer line's own increment, so the second row's index lands at 2, past the last row. The component work unit's report records a separate reference defect at `src/index.tsx:507-515`.

presentation.title: Reference defects need a disposition
presentation.synopsis: The reference-case criterion allows only carried-over cases or differences caused by `similar`, but some reference expectations are defects.
presentation.context:
Re-orienting: the reference-case acceptance criterion.
Catch-up:
- Where: WORK:crit-rdjdbfyxnt (reference cases).
- Purpose: account for every TypeScript test case.
- Situation: three cases expect a changed-row index past the last row.
- Goal: defects recorded as such, never ported.
presentation.key_points:
- `diffLines` of [0, 2] over two rows comes from a counter overcount.
- The criterion offers no honest home for such a case.
presentation.resolution_points: - `name-the-cause`: reword the criterion to "Each reference case in `test/compute-lines-test.ts` is carried over, or recorded as differing with its cause: `similar`'s alignment or a defect in the reference."
presentation.substance: Test coverage and contract correctness: keeps a reference defect from being ported.
presentation.specificity_reasoning: The criterion enumerates dispositions and misses one.

addressed_details.response: WORK:crit-rdjdbfyxnt (reference cases) now accepts a defect in the reference as a recorded cause beside `similar`'s alignment, so the reference changed-row overcount is recorded as a defect rather than ported.

content: Porting line by line from `src/compute-lines.ts` carries hazards the requirements do not repeat: the changed-row counter overcounts after a modified pair; empty removed lines get a one-space placeholder, which is presentation; and `similar` line tokens keep their terminators (`\n`, `\r\n`, or a bare `\r`), so lines compared as `similar` tokenizes them would misalign text that differs only in its ending; REQT-hmsfnfe5wc (Line marking) compares lines without terminators, and REQT-rtwn1qresp (Line ending changes) still needs each side's terminator kept.
evidence: `src/compute-lines.ts:197-211` with `:251` (counter increments), `:192` (`line || ' '`), and `similar-3.2.0/src/text/abstraction.rs:164-190` (terminators, including a bare `\r`, kept in line tokens). The scratch probe of `TextDiff::from_lines` returned values such as `test\n` and `a\n`. `.project/requirements/diff-viewer.reqts.md:67` and `:71` state line marking without terminators and line ending changes.

presentation.title: Reference porting hazards
presentation.synopsis: A row counter overcount, a one-space placeholder, and `similar`'s kept line terminators trap a line-by-line port.
presentation.context:
Re-orienting: hazards in the reference line computation.
Catch-up:
- Where: `src/compute-lines.ts`.
- Purpose: the TypeScript source the engine ports.
- Situation: its quirks are not requirements.
- Goal: the engine avoids importing them.
presentation.key_points:
- The changed-row counter overcounts after a modified pair (`src/compute-lines.ts:197-211`, `:251`).
- `line || ' '` is display padding (`:192`).
- `similar` line tokens keep their terminators, so alignment must compare lines without them while line ending changes keep each side's terminator.
presentation.resolution_points: - `worker-hazard-list`: keep this advice open as the worker's hazard list.
presentation.substance: Contract correctness: each hazard produces wrong output if ported.
presentation.specificity_reasoning: Hazard context for the worker, not design material.

addressed_details.response: All three hazards are avoided, each guarded by a test. The changed-row counter is not ported: WORK:activity-6aywz75j6h (Changed-line positions) reports real entry positions, and the reference's overcount is recorded as a reference defect beside the cases expecting it, per WORK:crit-rdjdbfyxnt. The one-space placeholder is not ported: an empty line keeps its empty text, since padding is presentation ARCH-jf3s5npp9s (LineDiffEngine) excludes. The kept terminators are handled by splitting lines in the crate rather than through `similar`'s line tokenizer, so REQT-hmsfnfe5wc (Line marking) compares line text while REQT-rtwn1qresp (Line ending changes) keeps each side's terminator.

content:
Activity development:
- Changed-line positions (WORK:activity-6aywz75j6h): positions identify the entries of the paired line information that hold a change, so the component can fold in either view; a narrower reading as one side's line numbers misses added-only and removed-only entries.

Set aside as unanchored:
- Whether apps may call the engine directly for line information without the component; nothing in the mission, epic, or requirements asks for it.
evidence: `src/compute-lines.ts:33-36` and `:184-187` return changed positions as indexes into `lineInformation`. `.project/requirements/diff-viewer.reqts.md:91` folds unchanged lines by distance from every change, which the component computes over paired entries.

content: REQT-dqxm8fa7ts (Modified lines) pairs removed lines immediately followed by added lines; `similar` might report insertions before deletions inside one change block, leaving such lines unpaired.
evidence: `similar-3.2.0/src/algorithms/replace.rs:5-10` states that text diffing uses the Replace hook to keep a consistent order of inserts and deletes; `:56-70` flushes a held deletion before a held insertion. The scratch probe listed Delete before Insert in every mixed block.

addressed_details.response: No change needed: within a change block `similar` reports deletions before insertions, so the pairing rule in REQT-dqxm8fa7ts always sees the removed lines first.

content: The compare method and trailing whitespace requirements might diverge from what `similar` provides: its word tokens, its default alignment algorithm, and whole-text trimming.
evidence: `similar-3.2.0/src/text/abstraction.rs:213-229` splits text into alternating whitespace and non-whitespace runs, matching REQT-xzc8n354h1 (Word comparison). `similar-3.2.0/src/text/mod.rs:367-378` makes Myers the default algorithm, the plain reading of alignment as `similar`'s line diff aligns them. `src/compute-lines.ts:149-151` trims each whole text's end, matching REQT-9tze98pt6g (Trailing whitespace).

addressed_details.response: No change needed: each requirement states behavior that `similar`'s defaults or a whole-text trim deliver directly.

- Asked which instructions pointed at consent and maturity, the review traced consent to REQT-2mge0tjtxq (Greenfield Work-Ready) condition (a), and the maturity move to an inference joining the pre-work rule that unrecorded expectations stay unclosed with the requirements consumer's check for `consented` maturity; the Work Planner's unsteered-draft rule and the maturity schema point the other way.

- The finding was presented ahead of the candidate architecture finding because the architecture records and the Rust Tester test drafts both carry the crate name.

- The stakeholder accepted centralized placement in `.project/architecture/` and the proposed candidate records.
- The Architect judged the engine's architecture well understood, so the records are detailed before work and bind the worker, while staying DREAMED.

- The stakeholder accepted the reworded criterion as proposed.
- The review re-traced the overcount before presenting: jsdiff merges consecutive added tokens into one change, so the nested call for the paired added line and the outer removed line each increment the row counter, placing the second row's index at 2.
- The Rust Tester will draft those three reference cases with engine-computed expectations and the defect cause beside each.

- The stakeholder judged the advice a minor-detail finding that should never have been filed, and asked whether its substance had been checked before presentation.
- The architecture written an hour after this filing already carries the contract it asks for, so the expectation was closed in the records and the remaining difference was activity wording, which pre-work leaves as consented (REQT-dbh4p81act).

body:
**Commits**
- `4eb9d2a`: settles the reference-case criterion, the porting-hazard wording, and the changed-line positions advice.

**Decisions**
- Reference cases whose expectation is a reference defect are recorded as differing with that cause, rather than carried over or blamed on `similar`.
- The changed-line positions advice was dismissed rather than acted on: ARCH-exgfx6rwdt (LineDiff) and ARCH-jf3s5npp9s (LineDiffEngine) already state that positions index the entries holding a change.
- The drafted tests assert observable output. The character-comparison test asserts which character is marked rather than the whole token split, since splitting is `similar`'s business, not a requirement.

**Blockers and stubs**
- `rust-dioxus/tests/line_diff_engine.rs` does not compile until the crate exists; the first activity establishes it. The file names a provisional entry point (`line_diff`, `LineDiffOptions`, `LineDiff`) drawn from the architecture records, and its header says the worker owns the exact spelling.

**For the reviewer**
- The coverage map is the test names: each carries the REQT id it covers, so post-work can check every in-scope child requirement against one named test.
- Four reference cases expect a changed-row index past the last row. They are recorded as a reference defect in the reference-case test, with the source lines named beside them.

**For the next worker**
- The overcount in the reference comes from jsdiff merging consecutive added tokens into one change: the nested call for the paired added line and the outer removed line each increment the row counter (`src/compute-lines.ts:197-211`, `:251`).
- `similar`'s line tokenizer keeps `\n`, `\r\n`, and a bare `\r` inside each line token (`~/.cargo/registry/src/*/similar-3.2.0/src/text/abstraction.rs:164-190`), which is why line identity has to drop terminators while REQT-rtwn1qresp (Line ending changes) still needs them.
- `.project/` is a plain git worktree on branch `project` with no `.weaver/` tooling, so the weave gates have nothing to run; commit inside it with `git -C .project`.

**Commits**
- `28289d6`: the crate, the engine, and the drafted tests brought up to passing.
- `6d53a74`: a test holding the engine to leaving out the reference's one-space padding.

**Decisions**
- This crate splits lines itself rather than using `similar`'s line tokenizer, so alignment compares line text while each terminator stays available for the line ending change.
- `DiffOp::Replace` does the modified-line pairing: its overlapping old and new runs become the pairs, and the leftover lines fall out as plain removals or additions.
- Entry text is an owned `String` rather than a borrow of the input texts, because a Dioxus component holds this output in state across renders, which needs `'static`.
- No `tracing` dependency and no instrumentation: the engine is a pure function with no I/O and no failure case, so instrumenting it would be entry and exit spam.
- Inline tokens are left unmerged: the pre-work word-comparison test fixes unmerged tokens, and same-kind runs are recoverable from tokens while tokens are not recoverable from runs.

**Observations**
- The pre-work test helpers returned a three-part tuple that clippy's `type_complexity` flagged; a `Row` alias now carries it. Low severity, resolved in the same commit.
- The two property tests run over fixed case lists rather than generated inputs, which is the shape the pre-work strategy drafted and the sign-off approved. Whether these invariants deserve generator-driven coverage is a live question for post-work, not a gap against the consented plan. Low severity.

**For the reviewer**
- Three tests carry the reference-case accounting, each named for its disposition: all nine cases in one table, the reference's changed-row overcount, and the character-token granularity difference.
- Every in-scope child requirement is covered by the test whose doc comment carries its REQT id, as the pre-work strategy laid out.
- The first acceptance criterion is checkable from `LineDiff` alone: each entry carries both sides with their numbers, the change kind, inline tokens, and any ending change, and `changed_positions` gives folding its distances.
- `cargo test` (19 passing), `cargo clippy --all-targets` (clean), and `cargo fmt --check` all pass in `rust-dioxus/`.
- The acceptance criteria are left unchecked deliberately; verifying them is post-work's own step.

**For the next worker**
- The crate root is `rust-dioxus/` itself: its `Cargo.toml` names the package `dioxus-diff-viewer`, and no workspace sits above it.
- Builds land in `/home/san/dev/.cargo-target` through the user's cargo config rather than `rust-dioxus/target`, so that is where artifacts are.
- `dioxus` is deliberately absent from the dependencies; the component work unit adds it, which keeps engine test compiles fast.
- The reference records an added-only row as an empty `left` object while the engine records an absent old side, which is why the reference-case table asserts `None` there.
- Unmerged inline tokens mean character comparison hands the component one token per character, where the reference handed it one per run. Merging adjacent same-kind tokens for rendering is the component's call and is a pure function of what the engine already returns.

Deliverable verification passed on the reference-case criterion, the unchanged-TypeScript criterion, the nine in-scope child requirements, the worker's test and lint claims, the provisional-identifier sweep, the pointer check, and the glossary sweep; the engine-output-alone criterion passed except for the gap in AUDIT:finding-3tvc9b4x0m. location: In EntryBuilder::push (appends one entry and records its position when it holds a change) at rust-dioxus/src/line_diff_engine.rs:236-241
observation: `changed_positions` records a position only when `entry.change != ChangeKind::Unchanged`, so an unchanged pair carrying a line ending change is absent from it. The component folds by distance from the positions in `changed_positions` (REQT-qcnxhemvhn, Folded unchanged lines) and must show each side's terminator as a chip (REQT-4zyjfjrhd3, Line ending chips), so an isolated line ending change is folded away and can never be seen.
evidence: rust-dioxus/src/line_diff_engine.rs:236-241 gates the `changed_positions.push` on `entry.change != ChangeKind::Unchanged`, and rust-dioxus/src/line_diff_engine.rs:187 sets `line_ending_change` on unchanged pairs. A scratch probe of `line_diff("a\rb", "a\nb", ...)` at the capture-time check returned entry 0 as Unchanged with `line_ending_change: Some(("\r", "\n"))` and `changed_positions: []`. ARCH-exgfx6rwdt (LineDiff) states the output holds `positions of entries holding a change` and lists REQT-qcnxhemvhn among its supported requirements (.project/architecture/dioxus-diff-viewer.arch.md:220-232). .project/requirements/diff-viewer.reqts.md:71 requires the pair be marked as carrying a line ending change, and :77 requires the chip in both views. The work unit's tests assert the ending change itself (rust-dioxus/tests/line_diff_engine.rs:208-229) but never assert its position.

presentation.title: Line ending changes are missing from changed_positions
presentation.synopsis: An unchanged pair carrying a line ending change is absent from changed_positions, so folding hides it and its chip never shows.
presentation.context:
Re-orienting: the engine's changed_positions, which the component folds by.
Catch-up:
- Where: EntryBuilder::push, rust-dioxus/src/line_diff_engine.rs:236-241.
- Purpose: tells the component where the changes sit.
- Situation: a line ending change lands on a pair marked unchanged.
- Goal: every entry a reader must see stays out of a fold.
presentation.key_points:
- An unchanged pair may carry a line ending change (line_diff_engine.rs:187).
- changed_positions gates on the change kind alone (line_diff_engine.rs:236-241).
- REQT-qcnxhemvhn (Folded unchanged lines) folds unchanged lines far from every change.
- REQT-4zyjfjrhd3 (Line ending chips) needs the chip visible in both views.
- ARCH-exgfx6rwdt (LineDiff) calls these the positions of entries holding a change.
presentation.resolution_points:
- `ending-change-counts-as-change`: record the position when the entry is not unchanged or carries a line ending change, and assert it in a test. The entry keeps ChangeKind::Unchanged, so neither view's marking shifts.
- `component-scans-entries`: leave the engine as it is and have the component scan every entry for an ending change while folding; demoted because ARCH-exgfx6rwdt (LineDiff) makes changed_positions the folding input and WORK:crit-113mtz82xb requires folding from the engine's output alone.
presentation.substance: Contract correctness and requirements coverage: an isolated line ending change becomes unreachable in the component, failing REQT-4zyjfjrhd3 (Line ending chips) and weakening WORK:crit-113mtz82xb (engine output alone).
presentation.actionability: Workable: one condition in EntryBuilder::push plus a test asserting the position.
presentation.specificity_reasoning: ARCH-exgfx6rwdt (LineDiff) states what changed_positions holds in words that do not settle whether a line ending change counts as a change; the design material leaves the case unstated.

location: In split_lines (splits a text into lines, holding each terminator aside) at rust-dioxus/src/line_diff_engine.rs:100-139, against ARCH-atczcqvdsz (Line diff hand-off) in .project/architecture/dioxus-diff-viewer.arch.jsonl
observation: The engine does its own line tokenization and hands `similar` only the line texts, which is the choice that makes line identity ignore terminators while keeping each terminator available. The architecture says only that the engine asks `similar` for alignment; no decision record carries the own-tokenizer choice or the LineDiff structure the implementation settled on, so plan, implementation, and architectural capture disagree.
evidence: rust-dioxus/src/line_diff_engine.rs:6-10 and :100-139 implement the crate's own line splitting, and :40 passes pre-split line texts to `TextDiff::from_slices`. .project/architecture/dioxus-diff-viewer.arch.md:180-190 (ARCH-atczcqvdsz, Line diff hand-off) states `the engine asks similar for alignment` with no mention of tokenization ownership, and :247-262 (ARCH:dcisn-wma0h4mndz) records only the engine-versus-component split. The choice is recorded in WORK:report-d70x7f2ecw under Decisions, which the Evidence rule of architect.AUDIT.post-work.md forbids as the resting place for architectural capture. ARCH-kjjykjtt5r (PairedLineEntry) names `inline change tokens` and `line ending change` without the token-kind and per-side structure the code settled (rust-dioxus/src/line_diff_output.rs:37-75).

presentation.title: The engine's own line tokenization is uncaptured
presentation.synopsis: The engine splits lines itself and hands similar only line texts; the architecture still says only that the engine asks similar for alignment.
presentation.context:
Re-orienting: the line diff hand-off record against the engine's tokenization.
Catch-up:
- Where: ARCH-atczcqvdsz (Line diff hand-off) in dioxus-diff-viewer.arch.jsonl.
- Purpose: names how the engine and similar divide the work.
- Situation: the engine kept tokenization and gave similar only line texts.
- Goal: the architecture reads as what was built.
presentation.key_points:
- split_lines is the engine's own tokenizer (line_diff_engine.rs:100-139).
- That choice is what lets line identity ignore terminators.
- ARCH-atczcqvdsz (Line diff hand-off) says only that the engine asks similar for alignment.
- The reason lives in WORK:report-d70x7f2ecw, which the Architect's evidence rule excludes as architectural capture.
- ARCH-kjjykjtt5r (PairedLineEntry) omits the token-kind and per-side structure that shipped.
presentation.resolution_points: - `capture-the-tokenization-decision`: add a decision record for the engine's own line tokenization, carrying the tension that similar keeps terminators inside line tokens and the consequence that line identity compares text alone; amend ARCH-atczcqvdsz (Line diff hand-off) to say the engine hands similar pre-split line texts; extend ARCH-kjjykjtt5r (PairedLineEntry) at gesture altitude to name the per-side inline tokens and their kinds.
presentation.substance: Maintainability and contract correctness: a next worker reading the architecture would take similar's line tokenizer as the alignment input and reintroduce the terminator hazard WORK:advice-nj1vrndsnf named.
presentation.actionability: Workable: one decision record and two field amendments in the existing architecture file.
presentation.specificity_reasoning: ARCH-atczcqvdsz (Line diff hand-off) states the hand-off's payload and trigger but leaves the division of tokenization unstated.

location: In LineSide.text and InlineToken.text (the text each output record carries) at rust-dioxus/src/line_diff_output.rs:32 and :53, produced at rust-dioxus/src/line_diff_engine.rs:167, :176, and :285-304
observation: Every line text and every inline token is an owned `String` copied out of the input texts, and an unchanged inline token is copied twice, once per side. Under the default character comparison a modified line allocates roughly two `String`s per character. A feasible restructuring exists: the output could borrow from the input texts through a lifetime parameter or carry `Cow<'_, str>`, and a shared `Arc<str>` of each input text with per-side ranges would keep the output `'static` for Dioxus state while removing every copy.
evidence: rust-dioxus/src/line_diff_output.rs:6-8 states the owned-text choice and its reason; :32 and :53 declare `text: String`. rust-dioxus/src/line_diff_engine.rs:167 and :176 call `line.text.to_owned()` per side, and :285-295 call `change.value().to_owned()` per token with a further `text.clone()` for each unchanged token. rust-dioxus/src/line_diff_engine.rs:33-34 shows the inputs are borrowed `&str`, so the line texts are already subslices of them. rust-coder.AUDIT.post-work.md Lens 1 asks whether a feasible restructuring would eliminate the copy and states that written justifications do not discharge the finding. No requirement or acceptance criterion names ownership; the only source for the choice is the module header and WORK:report-d70x7f2ecw.

presentation.title: Every line text and inline token is copied
presentation.synopsis: The output owns copies of text already held as subslices of the inputs; character comparison allocates about two Strings per character.
presentation.context:
Re-orienting: text ownership in the engine's output.
Catch-up:
- Where: LineSide.text and InlineToken.text, rust-dioxus/src/line_diff_output.rs:32 and :53.
- Purpose: carries each line's and each token's text to the component.
- Situation: the inputs are borrowed and their subslices are copied out.
- Goal: the component holds the output across renders without per-character allocation.
presentation.key_points:
- to_owned runs per side (line_diff_engine.rs:167, :176) and per token (:285-295).
- An unchanged token is cloned once for each side.
- The stated reason is that Dioxus state needs 'static.
- An Arc<str> of each input with per-side ranges keeps 'static and drops the copies.
- Rusty's zero-copy lens says a written justification does not discharge the finding.
presentation.resolution_points:
- `record-the-ownership-tradeoff`: keep the owned text as shipped and record the tradeoff on ARCH-kjjykjtt5r (PairedLineEntry), so the choice stops reading as an unexamined default and the component work unit inherits it deliberately.
- `share-the-input-texts`: carry each input text as an Arc<str> in the LineDiff with per-side byte ranges, keeping the output 'static while removing every copy; demoted because it changes the public shape WORK-6ds59btb76 (Diff viewer Dioxus component) is already planned against, and no measurement yet shows the allocation matters.
presentation.substance: Maintainability and performance: the allocation grows with text size on every recomputation, and the ownership shape is public, so changing it later reaches the component.
presentation.actionability: Workable either way: a recorded tradeoff, or a change to the output types before the component depends on them.
presentation.specificity_reasoning: ARCH-exgfx6rwdt (LineDiff) and ARCH-kjjykjtt5r (PairedLineEntry) describe the output's content without stating ownership, so the material left the choice to the worker.

location: In LineDiffOptions.inline_changes (the consumer's on-or-off choice) at rust-dioxus/src/line_diff_options.rs:25, against PairedLineEntry.inline_changes (the tokens themselves) at rust-dioxus/src/line_diff_output.rs:89
observation: One spelling visible outside its module carries two semantics: on the options it is the consumer's choice whether to compute inline changes, on the entry it is the computed inline changes. The option is also a bare `bool` at a public interface, where a two-variant enum would say at each call site which way the switch points.
evidence: rust-dioxus/src/line_diff_options.rs:23-25 declares `pub inline_changes: bool` with the doc `Whether modified lines carry the tokens removed and added within them`; rust-dioxus/src/line_diff_output.rs:86-89 declares `pub inline_changes: Option<InlineChanges>` as the tokens. Both are public through rust-dioxus/src/lib.rs:13-16. code-whisperer.SKILL.md Naming Stewardship item 7 forbids one spelling carrying two semantics for any name visible outside its module. rust-coder.SKILL.md Specific Patterns prescribes replacing a `bool` parameter with a two-variant enum. The tests show the call-site reading: `inline_changes: false` at rust-dioxus/tests/line_diff_engine.rs:127, :150, :186, and six further sites. REQT-4nz35dscrn (Inline changes) names the behavior but not the option's spelling.

presentation.title: inline_changes names both the switch and the tokens
presentation.synopsis: One public spelling carries two semantics, and the option is a bare bool where a two-variant enum would read at the call site.
presentation.context:
Re-orienting: the inline changes option against the inline changes field.
Catch-up:
- Where: LineDiffOptions.inline_changes, rust-dioxus/src/line_diff_options.rs:25.
- Purpose: lets the consumer turn inline changes off.
- Situation: PairedLineEntry.inline_changes holds the tokens under the same name.
- Goal: one spelling, one semantic, readable at every call site.
presentation.key_points:
- Both names are public through lib.rs:13-16.
- Naming Stewardship forbids one spelling carrying two semantics beyond its module.
- `inline_changes: false` appears at nine call sites in the tests.
- Rusty prescribes a two-variant enum in place of a public bool.
presentation.resolution_points:
- `name-the-switch-by-its-question`: rename the option to `mark_inline_changes` and leave PairedLineEntry.inline_changes as the tokens, which separates the two semantics in one rename.
- `two-variant-enum`: replace the bool with an InlineChanges enum of Marked and Unmarked; demoted because that name collides with the output struct InlineChanges and would need its own naming pass first.
presentation.substance: Maintainability: these public names are the contract the component and downstream apps read, and renaming after they depend on it is costly.
presentation.actionability: Workable: one field rename and nine call sites in the tests.
presentation.specificity_reasoning: The crate's public vocabulary was settled at WORK:advice-98x4z0fcpf to follow the requirement terms; REQT-4nz35dscrn (Inline changes) names the behavior and leaves the option's own spelling unstated.

location: In the Properties section (the two tests asserting invariants over the engine's output) at rust-dioxus/tests/line_diff_engine.rs:527-607
observation: Both tests under the Properties heading iterate a hard-coded list of three to five input pairs, so they are example tests wearing a property's name. The invariants they state, that each side's line texts rejoin to that side's trimmed input and that each side's numbers run contiguously from the offset, hold over all inputs and are exactly the shape generated inputs would exercise.
evidence: rust-dioxus/tests/line_diff_engine.rs:534-540 and :572-576 declare fixed `cases` vectors; no generator or shrinking is involved and the crate's Cargo.toml:7-8 carries no dev-dependency. rust-tester.SKILL.md Property-Based Testing names `proptest` and `quickcheck` for exactly this, and its Advanced Testing Tools table lists `proptest` for invariant validation and edge case discovery. WORK:report-d70x7f2ecw records the same observation under Observations and states the question belongs to post-work rather than to the consented plan. WORK:advice-zaj371p040 drafted them as `property tests` without naming a generator, so the delivered shape matches the approved pre-work strategy.

presentation.title: The property tests run fixed cases, not generated ones
presentation.synopsis: Both tests under the Properties heading iterate a hard-coded list, so universal invariants are checked on three to five inputs.
presentation.context:
Re-orienting: the two invariant tests closing the engine's suite.
Catch-up:
- Where: rust-dioxus/tests/line_diff_engine.rs:527-607.
- Purpose: hold the rejoin and contiguous-numbering invariants over all inputs.
- Situation: each iterates a hard-coded list of three to five text pairs.
- Goal: the invariants exercised by inputs no author chose.

- No generator or dev-dependency is involved (Cargo.toml:7-8).
- Both invariants hold over all inputs, which is what generators are for.
- The worker recorded the same observation and handed the question to post-work.

location: In the test suite as a whole (rust-dioxus/tests/line_diff_engine.rs), against split_lines at rust-dioxus/src/line_diff_engine.rs:106-139 and the error-free contract of ARCH-atczcqvdsz (Line diff hand-off)

The suite was drawn from the reference cases and the requirement statements, so input shapes outside both went uncovered.
evidence:
rust-dioxus/src/line_diff_engine.rs:113-120 treats a lone `` as a terminator, and :102-105 documents the intent. A search of rust-dioxus/tests/line_diff_engine.rs for a bare `` case and for `line_diff(""` returned no matches at the capture-time check; the terminator tests at :107-121 and :208-229 both use `
` against `
`. A scratch probe at the capture-time check confirmed the behavior is already correct: `line_diff("ab", "a
b", ...)` reports the ending change as `("", "
")`, `line_diff("", "")` yields no entries, and `line_diff("", "abc")` yields one added entry. .project/requirements/diff-viewer.reqts.md:77 names `` among the chip values.

presentation.title: Bare carriage return and empty texts have no test
presentation.synopsis: The engine handles a lone carriage return and an empty text on either side, and no test asserts either behavior.
presentation.context:
Re-orienting: input shapes outside the reference cases and the requirement statements.
Catch-up:
- Where: rust-dioxus/tests/line_diff_engine.rs as a whole.
- Purpose: hold the engine to what its code and architecture promise.
- Situation: split_lines recognizes a lone carriage return and the suite never uses one.
- Goal: every deliberately handled input shape has a test.

location: In CompareMethod (the consumer's choice of how a modified line's two texts are compared) at rust-dioxus/src/line_diff_options.rs:6-16
observation: `CompareMethod` is a public enum the project already expects to grow, and it carries no `#[non_exhaustive]`, so a consumer's exhaustive match breaks when a fourth method lands. `ChangeKind` and `TokenKind` are closed by their requirements and are not part of this.
evidence: rust-dioxus/src/line_diff_options.rs:6-16 declares the three variants with no `#[non_exhaustive]`, and rust-dioxus/src/lib.rs:13 exports it. WORK:advice-rpqenvbxcb records that README.md:151-165 lists seven jsdiff compare methods while the requirements define three, with the mapping of the other four carried by WORK-6ds59btb76 (Diff viewer Dioxus component), so growth is anticipated rather than speculative. rust-coder.SKILL.md Specific Patterns prescribes `#[non_exhaustive]` for types likely to change. REQT-hmsfnfe5wc (Line marking) and REQT-4nz35dscrn (Inline changes) enumerate the marks and token kinds exhaustively, which is why the other two enums are excluded here.

presentation.title: CompareMethod is exhaustive and expected to grow
presentation.synopsis: Four more compare methods are anticipated and the enum carries no non_exhaustive, so a consumer's exhaustive match breaks when one lands.
presentation.context:
Re-orienting: how the compare method enum grows.
Catch-up:
- Where: rust-dioxus/src/line_diff_options.rs:6-16.
- Purpose: the consumer's choice of how a modified line's texts are compared.
- Situation: three of the reference's seven methods are offered so far.
- Goal: adding a fourth does not break a consumer's match.
presentation.key_points:
- WORK:advice-rpqenvbxcb records the other four methods as the component unit's scope.
- Rusty prescribes non_exhaustive for types likely to change.
- ChangeKind and TokenKind are closed by their requirements and stay exhaustive.
presentation.resolution_points: - `mark-compare-method-non-exhaustive`: add #[non_exhaustive] to CompareMethod alone, which costs nothing inside the crate and keeps a later variant from breaking downstream apps.
presentation.substance: Maintainability: a breaking change for downstream apps is avoidable now at no cost, and not avoidable once apps depend on the enum.
presentation.specificity_reasoning: ARCH-n7wmjnmt65 (LineDiffOptions) names the three compare methods without saying whether the set is closed.
